blocks.x: Agentic SDLC inside delivery governance — cycle time down 34% and audit-ready evidence generated by the work itself
an IT services firm whose delivery governance was excellent and whose delivery was buried under evidence of it. Figures are the client's own, shared with permission.

The baseline sprint measured the paperwork: 31% of engineer time on status, documentation and audit artifacts, delivery evidence assembled retrospectively for every review, and client audit prep consuming a fortnight per program per quarter.
The governance demanded evidence the tooling couldn't produce. Engineers narrated what the pipeline could have recorded.

We moved the SDLC to governed agents with evidence as a by-product: work items decomposed with acceptance criteria machine-checkable, agents preparing code reviews and test scaffolds inside the delivery policy, every gate artifact generated from the actual work — commits, tests, reviews — and the client audit pack assembling itself continuously. Governance stopped being a tax on delivery; it became the record of it.
